one_liner: Header-only SIMD JSON DOM parser and serializer for C++ with a RapidJSON-style API, about 2x RapidJSON on nativejson-benchmark files.
what_it_does: Parses JSON into a mutable document tree (sonic_json::Document and Node) and serializes it back through a WriteBuffer. The API uses RapidJSON-like names: Parse, HasParseError, FindMember, MemberBegin, IsInt64/GetInt64, Set*, and a RapidJSON-style allocator concept. Beyond the plain DOM it offers ParseOnDemand (pull one value by a key path given at the call site), JSON Pointer access via AtPointer, a schema-filtered parse, and parse and serialize flags. It is not source-compatible with RapidJSON: the namespace, the types and the writer API differ.
how_it_is_fast: SIMD (AVX2/SSE, with NEON and SVE2 paths at HEAD) skips whitespace and finds quote and escape characters in strings during parsing, and finds characters that need escaping during serialization. A SAX-style handler builds a compact node tree whose objects store members in a vector, so building the tree is cheap. Numbers are parsed with Eisel-Lemire plus a decimal fallback (atof_native.h) and printed with the Schubfach algorithm (ftoa.h). ParseOnDemand uses SIMD and bit masks to skip values it does not need.
when_to_use: x86-64 Linux services on AVX2 hardware (Haswell or newer) that use the RapidJSON DOM today and want roughly 2x faster parsing and serialization with a familiar API.
Workloads that parse, modify and re-serialize documents (add, remove or set members) rather than only reading them.
Extracting one or a few fields by a known key path from large payloads with ParseOnDemand, which skips everything else.
Teams that want a header-only C++ library with no runtime dependencies and an Apache-2.0 licence.
when_not_to_use: Inputs that need UTF-8 validation: docs/usage.md says Sonic assumes UTF-8 and does not verify it, and the ParseFlags enum in flags.h has no validation flag.

Windows/MSVC, or macOS without checking first: the README supports only GCC or Clang on Linux; issue #133 asks whether it runs on macOS and #116 reports that the unit tests fail to compile on aarch64, although NEON, SVE2-128 and RISC-V code has landed since 2024.

When raw speed is the only criterion: in Sonic's own charts yyjson is at or above Sonic on 7 of 11 decode files and 6 of 11 encode files, simdjson parses faster on several files and on the nativejson chart, and yyjson serializes faster there.

Large objects queried many times: members are stored in a vector, so FindMember is a linear scan unless you call CreateMap to build a std::multimap index. Issue #86 reports string-heavy parsing performance about equal to RapidJSON (no numbers given).

Older checkouts on untrusted input: recent commits fixed a use-after-free in Stack::Reserve (2025-12-26), OOM handling (2026-04-23) and a bounded emoji-escape tail (2026-07-17); issue #111 reported an ASan heap-buffer-overflow read on a malformed nested input; issue #140 asks when the next release is.

integration.dependencies: none (benchmark and tests fetch Google Benchmark, GoogleTest, RapidJSON, yyjson, simdjson, cJSON and JsonCpp)
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (README); GCC or Clang compiled with -mavx2 -mpclmul -mbmi or -march=haswell (docs/usage.md); old GCC releases fail to build (issues #74 and #98, gcc 4.8.5)
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX2 on Linux is the documented target; the build files also have SSE4.2, NEON, SVE2-128 and RISC-V rv64gc/zbb options and an optional -DSONIC_DYNAMIC_DISPATCH=1 mode; MSVC is unsupported
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each Document owns its allocator by default, and re-parsing a Document invalidates pointers and iterators from the earlier parse (docs/usage.md)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: method names follow RapidJSON (Parse, HasParseError, FindMember, MemberBegin, GetString) and it reuses RapidJSON's allocator concept, but the namespace, types, writer and flags differ and RawNumber is missing, so call sites need porting

gotchas: Harness flaw in the project's own decode/encode benchmark: RapidJSON is built without RAPIDJSON_SSE2 or RAPIDJSON_SSE42. Neither the 2022 bazel/rapidjson.BUILD, the HEAD BUILD.bazel nor the CMake bench target defines them, so RapidJSON's SIMD whitespace-skip and string-scan code (reader.h) is compiled out while Sonic gets AVX2. nativejson-benchmark's rapidjsontest.cpp turns these on from __SSE2__/__SSE4_2__, which fits the smaller gap there (about 2.2x) against the own chart's 1.4x to 6x. The adapter also uses kParseNoFlags (no full-precision float parsing).

Harness flaw: the simdjson adapter keeps a dom::parser inside each ParseResult, and BM_Decode makes a new ParseResult every iteration, so simdjson re-allocates its parser buffers on every timed parse instead of reusing the parser. Its stat_impl and find_impl are stubs that return true, so the round-trip check after decoding verifies nothing for simdjson.

The round-trip correctness check is weak for every library: GetStats and find_value in the Sonic and RapidJSON adapters reset 'stat = DocStat()' on each recursive call, so stat1 != stat2 compares only the root counts plus the last subtree visited. The timings are unaffected, but a wrong parse would mostly go unnoticed.

Document::Parse copies the input into its own padded string buffer (allocateStringBuffer, SONICJSON_PADDING 64), and string nodes point into that buffer, so keep the Document alive while you use its strings. The README roadmap is stale: it lists JSON Pointer and JSON Path as missing, but AtPointer is documented and a 'support jsonpath' commit landed on 2026-03-25.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose Sonic over RapidJSON when you are on x86 AVX2 Linux and want a mutable DOM with near-RapidJSON call names plus on-demand path extraction. Choose yyjson (portable C, validates UTF-8, as fast or faster on most files in Sonic's own charts) or simdjson (faster parsing with UTF-8 validation) when portability, validation or read-only throughput matter more, and glaze when you are mapping JSON to C++ structs.
verified_claims_summary: These are first-party bar charts from 2022 (commit c16e355), with no CPU or compiler named. In the authors' nativejson-benchmark rerun on canada, citm_catalog and twitter, Sonic parses in about 1.0 ms against about 2.1 ms for RapidJSON and serializes in about 0.55 ms against about 1.2 ms (about 2.2x each); simdjson parses faster and yyjson serializes faster. The project's own Google Benchmark charts, normalized to Sonic, put RapidJSON at 0.16-0.74 on decode, but that RapidJSON build had its SSE paths compiled out.
status_note: Active ByteDance project (977 stars, last commit 2026-07-17, Apache-2.0, header-only and easy to vendor), but the performance charts date from 2022 and users are waiting for a new release (issue #140).
